title: Its efficacy is absolute and does not wait for consent
source_text: XXXVIII. Quapropter etiam dicunt efficaciam gratiae istius esse absolutam, respectu bonae actionis, nec pendere a consensu liberi arbitrii: quia ut bona actio sequatur, non expectat liberi arbitrii consensum, sed eum potenter efficit; utpote quae liberum sibi subjicit arbitrium, nequaquam vero ejus potestati subjicitur.
pass_a_gloss: XXXVIII. For which reason also they say that the efficacy of that grace is absolute, with respect to the good action, nor depends on the consent of free choice: because that the good action may follow, it does not wait for the consent of free choice, but powerfully effects it; as that which subjects free choice to itself, but in no way is subjected to its power.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXXVIII. For this reason they also say that this grace's efficacy is absolute with respect to the good action and does not hang on the consent of free choice. For the good action to follow, it does not wait for free choice to consent but brings about that consent by its power, since it brings free choice under itself and is in no way subject to free choice's power.

lemmas.gloss: the efficacy of that grace is absolute

lemmas.latin: non expectat liberi arbitrii consensum, sed eum potenter efficit
lemmas.gloss: does not wait for the consent of free choice, but powerfully effects it

choices.why: Kept as in I-XXX: grace whose efficacy comes from the grace itself, not from the consent that follows.
